title: docs(protocol): Support Windows states latest-only support, and the releases index closes the v17 line
body:
Fixes #25102
Clause-②: no

A docs-only PR. It executes the maintainer's ruling `6328214336` on #25102, **letter A, latest-only** (「25134 25092 25102 同意」). It changes two hand-written pages by +9 / -7 lines:
- `content/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility.mdx`;
- `content/docs/releases/index.mdx`. This is the releases index, not a per-release page. No file under `content/docs/releases/v17/**` or `v18/**` is touched.

It edits no code, workflow, gate, changeset or ADR, and it takes no release action.

## What the ruling binds, and what this PR does not do

- **Done (ruling item 1):** the Support Windows table is replaced by a latest-only statement. The previous MAJOR receives no fixes, and an application upgrades through ADR-0087's conversion layer and `os migrate meta`. The page links both.
- **Not done (ruling item 3):** no B (an on-demand security line) and no C (a two-branch model).
- **Not written (ruling item 2):** the emergency-branch option. The page names no emergency branch, no date or window, and no EE-specific promise.

## Support Windows: before and after

**Before** (`:153`-`:159` at `abc25a3536`):

```text
### Support Windows

| Version | Status | Support Level |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Current MAJOR (N) | **Active** | Full feature development, bug fixes, security patches |
| Previous MAJOR (N-1) | **Maintenance** | Critical bug fixes and security patches only |
| Older versions (N-2+) | **End of Life** | No support; upgrade recommended |
```

**After:** the heading text "Support Windows" is unchanged, so `#support-windows` still resolves (see *Inbound anchors* below). Then a lead sentence and five bullets, in the bold-lead bullet shape of the page's "SemVer Guarantees" and "Migration Guides" sections. Each clause and its source:

| Clause on the page | Source |
|:---|:---|
| **Only the current MAJOR receives fixes.** There is no maintenance line for an older MAJOR: compatibility across majors is carried by the conversion layer and migration chain (ADR-0087), not by patching old releases. | Ruling item 1. npm re-check below: no version line of ours has ever published again after a newer line shipped. |
| **The current MAJOR**: bug fixes and security patches ship in the next release cut from `main`. While the next MAJOR is in prerelease, every release cut from `main` is one of its prereleases on the pre-mode dist-tag (`next` on the v18 line), so a fix reaches `latest` only when that MAJOR goes GA. | `.github/workflows/release.yml`'s header: `npm publish` lives in one job, reachable only from a `push` to `main` and from the repair dispatch, and the repair "cannot mint a version". The card's fact 4 measured the consequence: between 17.7.0 and 18.0.0, `latest` received no fix. The page's own top callout already states the pre-mode half. The tag is written "the pre-mode dist-tag" because nothing fixes it: `changeset pre enter` takes the tag as an argument, v16 and v17 ran on `rc` and v18 on `next`, and `.github/workflows/cut-rc.yml:235` requires `tag: rc` for its own lane only. |
| **The previous MAJOR, and every older one**: receives no fixes, and no backport or maintenance release is promised. To take a fix, upgrade to the current MAJOR. | Ruling item 1. |
| **The conversion layer** (ADR-0087 D2): as the runtime loads your metadata, it converts the previous MAJOR's lossless changes (renames, alias removals, field moves) to the current shape and emits a deprecation notice per conversion. Those shapes keep loading after you move the runtime forward. It covers only the previous MAJOR and only lossless changes; `os migrate meta` carries everything else. | ADR-0087 D2: scope "losslessly mappable changes only — renames, alias removals, field moves, enum re-spellings"; window "N accepts N−1 shapes at load"; "emitting a structured deprecation notice per applied conversion"; "Semantic changes are excluded … it goes to D3". |
| **`os migrate meta`** (ADR-0087 D3): `--from N` replays the chain from the major your metadata was authored against (protocol 16 or later, the chain's floor) to the current one in a single pass, and lists the edits your source needs. With `--write` it writes the mechanical ones it can trace to one literal into your source files. It reads no database. `--stored` replays the same chain over one deployment's `sys_metadata` rows and, with `--apply`, rewrites the ones still carrying an older shape. Links: the CLI reference (`/docs/deployment/cli#os-migrate-meta---stored`) and Upgrading, "The metadata app". | ADR-0087 D3 (cross-major in one command). `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`: the `os migrate meta --stored` row of the Data migrations table (`:1252`) and the section's "division of labour" paragraph (`:1819`), which states what `--from N` and `--stored` each do. `--write` and `--apply`: the flag descriptions in `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/meta.ts`. The floor: `MIGRATION_SUPPORT_FLOOR = 16` (`packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template:79`) and `content/docs/upgrading.mdx:233`. |
| **Testing a MAJOR before it reaches `latest`**: `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` fails a pull request that declares a `major` bump outside Changesets pre mode and stands aside inside it, and a MAJOR declared in pre mode publishes only prereleases, on the pre-mode dist-tag, until pre mode exits. The v18 line used `next` (`18.0.0-next.0` … `18.0.0-next.5`) before 18.0.0. Install from that tag to run your app against a MAJOR before it becomes `latest`. | `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` at `origin/main` `459afea1f6`: `judge()` (`:678`-`:683`) returns `exempt` when `.changeset/pre.json` has `mode: 'pre'` (`:681`) and `enforce` otherwise (`:682`). The `exempt` case exits 0 (`:818`-`:826`), and the `enforce` case prints the refusal (`:828`). The RC EXEMPTION header (`:113`-`:120`) states the Changesets semantics: in pre mode "a `major` bump only ever produces a … PRE-RELEASE version — nothing final publishes until `changeset pre exit`". npm: `18.0.0-next.0` (2026-10-13) to `18.0.0-next.5` (2026-10-19), then `18.0.0` (2026-10-20). The page says the guard fails "a" pull request, not "any", and it does not say a MAJOR can be declared only in pre mode, because the guard's `allow-major` label escape hatch skips it outside pre mode (header `:122`-`:124`; the label is read live at `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml:1063`). |

The CLI binary is spelled `os`, as everywhere else on this page. `packages/cli/package.json` `bin` maps both `os` and `objectstack` to the same `./bin/run.js`, so this is the ruling's `objectstack migrate meta`.

## Premise re-checks (ruling item 1), verbatim, at `origin/main` `abc25a3536`

```text
$ git grep -n -iE "End of Life|security patches only|support window" origin/main -- content skills README.md
origin/main:content/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility.mdx:153:### Support Windows
origin/main:content/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility.mdx:158:| Previous MAJOR (N-1) | **Maintenance** | Critical bug fixes and security patches only |
origin/main:content/docs/protocol/backward-compatibility.mdx:159:| Older versions (N-2+) | **End of Life** | No support; upgrade recommended |
(exit 0)
```

```text
$ for p in @objectstack/spec @object-ui/core better-auth; do printf '%s: ' "$p"; curl -s "https://registry.npmjs.org/$p" | jq -r '.time | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("^[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+$")) | "\(.value) \(.key)"' | sort | awk '{split($2,v,"."); print v[1]"."v[2]}' | uniq | sort | uniq -d | tr '\n' ' '; echo; done
@objectstack/spec:
@object-ui/core:
better-auth: 1.4 1.5 1.6 1.7
(exit 0)
```

Both hold as the card states. Neither of ours prints a re-published line, and the `better-auth` positive control prints `1.4 1.5 1.6 1.7`.

The card's grep has no "maintenance" term, so a wider grep was run to catch another page that states a maintenance line. The pattern covered `maintenance (line|release|branch|mode|window|period)`, `previous major`, `N-1`, `LTS`, `long-term support`, `backport`, `older (major|versions)`, `end-of-life` and `EOL`, over `content skills README.md`. It found 13 lines; none states a support window or a maintenance line:
- the two lines above;
- a retry formula (`backoffMultiplier^(n-1)`);
- a database maintenance window;
- the auto-generated plugin-versioning schema reference;
- Node.js end-of-life in the 17.0 notes;
- five lines on metadata authored against an older or previous major, which describe the conversion window, the stored-row replay, or a meaning that changed across a major (`upgrading.mdx:23`, `:199`, `cli.mdx:1742`, `api/declarative-endpoints.mdx:266`, `protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx:1173`), plus the matching skill line `skills/objectstack-api/SKILL.md:201`;
- one unrelated `forms.mdx` hit.

So no other page joins the surface.

## Every other sentence changed (ruling items 3 and 4)

1. **`backward-compatibility.mdx:142`, the Migration Support callout's second sentence.** This PR's new upgrade clause would have contradicted it on the same page.
   - Before: "An automated `codemod` command is referenced in the migration guides but is not yet available; until then, combine `os doctor --scan-deprecations`, `os diff`, and the CHANGELOG migration notes (below) to upgrade across MAJOR versions."
   - After: "There is no `codemod` command either: to upgrade your metadata across MAJOR versions, run `os migrate meta` (see [Support Windows](#support-windows)), and use `os doctor --scan-deprecations`, `os diff`, and the CHANGELOG migration notes (below) for what it does not rewrite."
   - Why: the old sentence names doctor, diff and the CHANGELOG as *the* way across majors, ten lines above a section that now says an app upgrades through the conversion layer and `os migrate meta`.
   - Why "your metadata": `os migrate meta` rewrites metadata. It does not rewrite the TypeScript patterns `os doctor --scan-deprecations` reports, and the comment at `packages/cli/src/commands/doctor.ts:2683` explains why doctor's own hint must not point at it. So the sentence scopes the command to metadata and keeps doctor, diff and the CHANGELOG for the rest.
   - Its "referenced in the migration guides" clause was also false. `git grep -i codemod -- content/docs skills` outside `releases/` finds only this sentence. The CLI has no `codemod` command: `doctor-deprecation-hint-commands.test.ts:160`-`:162` asserts that `objectstack codemod v2-to-v3` and `os codemod` resolve to no command.
   - The first sentence of the callout is unchanged.
2. **`releases/index.mdx:22`, the v17 entry's trailing status.**
   - Before: "(current series: 17.7.0, released 2026-10-06)".
   - After: "(final release: 17.7.0)".
   - Why: the index labelled both v18 and v17 "current series", and the latest-only statement allows exactly one. "final release: X" is the index's own wording for a closed line: v16 "(final release: 16.1.0)", v15 "(final release: 15.1.1)", v14 "(final release: 14.8.0)". The v16 label was set the same way when that line closed (`a1ef2c9d63`, the day after 17.0.0 shipped).
   - Gate compatibility: `check-release-section-coverage.mjs` `indexCurrencyFindings` passes any trailing status that names the newest 17.x GA (17.7.0). `check-release-page-status.mjs` names both wordings as valid. `sync-release-index-currency.mjs` rewrites only a stale `current series:` field and never a `final release:` one, so the version step leaves this entry alone.
   - The release date is dropped to match the three sibling entries. It stays on the v17 page.

No other sentence changed. The rest of `backward-compatibility.mdx` was read in full at `BASE`, including the PR #22988 sentences: the 17.x launch-window rule, the v18 prerelease regime and the "When it stops applying" section. Each of them describes versioning history or the breaking-change regime, and none promises a fix to an earlier line, so all stay.

**Releases index (ruling item 4).** No sentence in `content/docs/releases/` promises a previous-major fix. The grep, at `abc25a3536`:

```text
git grep -n -i -E "maintenance|backport|security (fix|patch)|previous major|N-1\b|support(ed)? (window|line|policy|period)|end[- ]of[- ]life|\bLTS\b|long[- ]term|current series|final release|receives? (fixes|patches)|patch(es)? (for|to) (the )?(previous|older|17\.x|16\.x)" abc25a3536 -- content/docs/releases
```

It found 14 lines (exit 0):
- index entries `:21`-`:25`, the status labels;
- `v16.mdx:20`, `:21` and `:863`, which state that v16 is closed;
- `v17/17-0.mdx:91`, Node.js end-of-life;
- `v17/17-4.mdx:355`, a store `maintenance` key;
- `v17/17-7.mdx:60`, `:192`, `:563` and `:915`, which concern long-term agent memory.

The only contrary statement is the v17 "current series" label (item 2). `meta.json` holds page order only, and `implementation-status.mdx` matched nothing.

**Inbound anchors.** `git grep -n -i "#support-windows"` exits 1 in this repo and exits 1 in `../objectui` at `b014f5eea`; the control leg in `../objectui` exits 0. `git grep "backward-compatibility#"` finds one inbound fragment link, `releases/index.mdx:82`, which targets the launch-window anchor and is unchanged. The heading text is kept anyway, because links from outside both repositories cannot be enumerated.

## Acceptance notes

- **ADR-0087 D6 is not cited.** D6 reads "Every major is published to the `next` dist-tag at least one RC cycle before `latest`", but the ADR's 2026-07-15 as-built addendum lists "P3 — MCP tools + RC discipline (D6): deferred, evidence-gated", and npm `@objectstack/spec` does not follow it:
  - majors 8 to 15 published no prerelease version at all (0 in the registry). That was the pre-launch window, which the same addendum ratifies for 12 to 15.
  - 16 and 17 ran `-rc.N` prereleases (`16.0.0-rc.0` and `rc.1`; `17.0.0-rc.0` to `rc.6`), and the `rc` dist-tag still points at `17.0.0-rc.6`.
  - only 18 ran on `next`.

  So both prerelease clauses rest on `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, which holds today, and name `next` only as the v18 instance. Nothing found fixes which tag a future pre mode uses, so the page names none. Not filed: it is history, with no reach. Carrier: none.
- **Out of this PR's surface, reported to the seat and filed by it as #25148 (one card for both):**
  - `content/docs/releases/index.mdx:21` reads "(current series: 18.0.0, released 2026-10-19)". The 18.0.0 Version Packages commit `06cab4849a` is dated 2026-10-20T11:47Z, npm's `time["18.0.0"]` is 2026-10-20T12:51Z, and `releases/v18/18-0.mdx:3` says "published 2026-10-20".
  - `content/docs/releases/v17/index.mdx`'s status blockquote still says "A plain install now resolves 17.7.0" while `latest` is 18.0.0. That is a per-release page, which this PR does not edit.
- **Prose that quotes the old callout wording.** Three places paraphrase the `:142` sentence this PR rewrites: the comments at `packages/cli/src/commands/doctor.ts:2680` and `packages/cli/src/commands/doctor-deprecation-hint-commands.test.ts:18`, and the source note at `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json:1189`. Each quotes "not yet available"; the page now says there is no `codemod` command. None of them reads the page, and no gate compares them. The same `doctor.ts` comment still says both of `os migrate meta`'s writes are `--out` JSON snapshots, which predates `--write`. They are code and QA data, outside this PR's surface. Not filed. Carrier: none.
